title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. S is a base on which n is invertible. f: X -> S is a smooth curve, t is a section of X, and X* is the open part over which the covers are étale (it includes the complement of t; f°: X* -> S). We consider covers X' -> X, with a marked section t' over t, and a finite étale S-group scheme G acting so that X'|X* is a G_{X*}-torsor. The stabiliser G_{t'} acts faithfully on the tangent line T_{X'/S,t'}. Its image in Aut(T_{X'/S,t'}) = G_m is mu_n, which gives a canonical monomorphism i: mu_{n,S} -> G (the inertia, rigidified by the marked point). The torsor gives a class xi in H^0(S, R^1 f°_* f°^*G).

This page states the classification precisely.
- First category: triples (X', t', G). A morphism (X',t',G) -> (X'_1,t'_1,G_1) is a pair (X' -> X'_1, G -> G_1) compatible with the marked sections and the actions.
- Second category: systems (G, n, xi, i, T, k). Here G is a finite étale group scheme over S and n >= 1. xi is a section of R^1 f°_* G such that the torsors it defines (locally on S) are tamely ramified of order n along t. i: mu_{n,S} -> G is a monomorphism of groups. T is an invertible O_S-module and k: T^{⊗n} ≅ T_{X/S,t} is an isomorphism with the normal (tangent) line of t.
- Morphisms of the second category are defined ad hoc. A homomorphism G -> G_1 must induce on mu_n -> mu_{n_1} the map lambda -> lambda^{n/n_1}, so n_1 | n, together with compatible maps of the roots T.
- Claim, finished on the next page: the natural functor from the first category to the second is an equivalence.

In modern terms: tame G-covers of a pointed curve, branched along t, with a marked point over t, correspond to three pieces of data. These are the monodromy torsor on X*, the inertia embedding mu_n -> G, and an n-th root of the normal bundle N_t = T_{X/S,t}. The last is a relative 'tangential base point', i.e. the root-stack datum: T_{X'/S,t'} is canonically an n-th root of T_{X/S,t}.

The proof sketch would use Abhyankar's lemma and Grothendieck–Murre tame theory near t. The marked point t' kills automorphisms, so torsors can be glued even when G is non-abelian.

Purpose (next page): take G = mu_2 = {±1} and n = 2, over a base with 2 invertible. Take X = P(J) and X' = E an elliptic curve, with X = E/{±1} and t the image of the zero section. Then the double cover with given branch data is equivalent to the choice of a square root (T, k: T^{⊗2} ≅ T_{X,t}). Here T = Lie(E). This is a stacky/relative description of elliptic curves as double covers of a P^1-bundle, aimed at a moduli description of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.
errors: xi is written as a section of R^1 f_* (image) but must be R^1 f°_* f°^*G on X*; for non-abelian G this is only a sheaf of pointed sets. Gluing local torsors over S needs the rigidification by t', which is implicit.

The conditions on xi are stated only as 'tamely ramified of order n'. One also needs compatibility between the local monodromy of xi at t and i(mu_n): the inertia must equal i(mu_n), via the generator determined by k. Without this the functor is not essentially surjective onto the stated category. Presumably this is intended ('compatibles dans un sens évident').
The ad hoc definition of morphisms in the second category is left unfinished. In particular the induced map T -> T_1 with T^{⊗ n/n_1} ≅ T_1 compatible with k and k_1 is not spelled out.
n must be invertible on S (tameness). This is implicit; the application only uses n = 2 in characteristic ≠ 2.

ideas.what: Classification of tame G-covers of a relative curve totally/tamely ramified along a section with marked point, by (monodromy torsor on complement, inertia embedding mu_n -> G, n-th root of the normal bundle of the section)
ideas.modern_name: tame covers vs. root stacks / log étale covers; Abhyankar lemma in families; twisted curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Murre (LNM 208, 1971) for tame fundamental group; Cadman (2007), Abramovich–Vistoli, Olsson (log twisted curves, 2007) for root-stack formulation
ideas.where_published: SGA1 XIII and Grothendieck–Murre treat the tame fundamental group, but not this rigidified relative formulation with n-th root of normal bundle as far as I know

ideas.what: Canonical monomorphism mu_n -> G from the action of the stabiliser of the marked point on the tangent line T_{X'/S,t'} (rigidified inertia)
ideas.modern_name: inertia character / canonical generator of tame inertia via tangent space

ideas.what: Tangent line at a ramification point as an n-th root of the tangent line downstairs, used as rigidifying datum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points)

ideas.what: Application: elliptic curves as mu_2-covers of P(J) ramified at image of origin, with square root of T_{X,t} being Lie(E)
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass/Legendre-type description of M_{1,1} over Z[1/2] via double covers of P^1-bundles

missed.claim: A relative (over arbitrary S) equivalence of categories between pointed tame G-covers of a pointed curve and data (xi, i: mu_n -> G, T, k: T^{⊗n} ≅ N_t). This is essentially the root-stack / twisted-curve description of tame covers with tangential base points. It is formulated c. 1981, before Deligne's tangential base points (1989) and Cadman/Abramovich–Vistoli/Olsson (2000s).
missed.quote: T un Module inv. sur S, ... et k un isom T^{⊗n} ⥲ T_{X/S,t}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows Grothendieck using n-th roots of normal bundles as moduli data for tame covers, the core idea of root stacks, in his anabelian/moduli period. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, essentially correct equivalence anticipating the root-stack/tangential-base-point formalism for tame covers in families. However, the result is now standard (Abhyankar plus Grothendieck–Murre), and here it is only a tool for elliptic curves.
transcription_corrections: 'R^1 f_* \int^{\alpha}(\underline{G})' should read R^1 f°_* f°^*(\underline{G}).
'les cas locaux (local. sur S)) des X grilles doit soient modérément ramifiés d'ordre n' likely reads 'les revêtements (localement sur S) de X* qu'il définit soient modérément ramifiés d'ordre n'.
'(...) des t' is 'le long de t'.
'de groupes' completes 'i: mu_{n,S} -> G est un monomorphisme ... de groupes'.
'où la définition ad hoc' is likely 'avec la définition ad hoc des morphismes'.
The NB line reads approximately 'G -> G_1 doit induire un homomorphisme mu_{n,S} -> mu_{n_1,S}, qui soit l'homomorphisme lambda -> lambda^{n/n_1}'.
The second category tuple includes i, i.e. (G, n, xi, i, T, k); the overwritten symbols in the image hide the i.
